    13 — Charts & map decorations¶

    This notebook demos the remaining earthkit-plots primitives just added to Digital-Earth — all wired onto cleopatra/pyramids, all runnable offline on synthetic data:

    • Charts (digitalearth.charts): line, bar, histogram.
    • Map decorations (Map): quiverkey, text / annotate at lon/lat, stock_img backdrop.
    • Layout (digitalearth.scene): grid multi-panel + shared_colorbar.

    Setup¶

    Imports and a small synthetic field over Europe (EPSG:4326) plus a u/v wind pair.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    %matplotlib inline
import numpy as np
from pyramids.dataset import Dataset, GeoReference
from digitalearth import charts
from digitalearth.scene import Map, grid, shared_colorbar

# A smooth synthetic field on a lon/lat grid covering Europe (-10..50 E, 30..70 N).
ny, nx = 80, 120
lon = np.linspace(-10, 50, nx)[None, :]
lat = np.linspace(70, 30, ny)[:, None]
field = (np.cos(np.deg2rad(lat)) * 20 + 10 * np.sin(np.deg2rad(lon * 3))).astype('float32')
GEO = (-10.0, 0.5, 0.0, 70.0, 0.0, -0.5)
FIELD = Dataset.from_array(arr=field, geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO, epsg=4326))

# A coarse u/v wind pair on the same region for the quiver demo.
ny2, nx2 = 16, 24
la = np.linspace(70, 30, ny2)[:, None] * np.ones((1, nx2))
lo = np.linspace(-10, 50, nx2)[None, :] * np.ones((ny2, 1))
GEO2 = (-10.0, 2.5, 0.0, 70.0, 0.0, -2.5)
U = Dataset.from_array(arr=np.cos(np.deg2rad(la)).astype('float32'), geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO2, epsg=4326))
V = Dataset.from_array(arr=(0.4 * np.sin(np.deg2rad(lo))).astype('float32'), geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO2, epsg=4326))
print('field:', FIELD.rows, 'x', FIELD.columns)
    %matplotlib inline import numpy as np from pyramids.dataset import Dataset, GeoReference from digitalearth import charts from digitalearth.scene import Map, grid, shared_colorbar # A smooth synthetic field on a lon/lat grid covering Europe (-10..50 E, 30..70 N). ny, nx = 80, 120 lon = np.linspace(-10, 50, nx)[None, :] lat = np.linspace(70, 30, ny)[:, None] field = (np.cos(np.deg2rad(lat)) * 20 + 10 * np.sin(np.deg2rad(lon * 3))).astype('float32') GEO = (-10.0, 0.5, 0.0, 70.0, 0.0, -0.5) FIELD = Dataset.from_array(arr=field, geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO, epsg=4326)) # A coarse u/v wind pair on the same region for the quiver demo. ny2, nx2 = 16, 24 la = np.linspace(70, 30, ny2)[:, None] * np.ones((1, nx2)) lo = np.linspace(-10, 50, nx2)[None, :] * np.ones((ny2, 1)) GEO2 = (-10.0, 2.5, 0.0, 70.0, 0.0, -2.5) U = Dataset.from_array(arr=np.cos(np.deg2rad(la)).astype('float32'), geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO2, epsg=4326)) V = Dataset.from_array(arr=(0.4 * np.sin(np.deg2rad(lo))).astype('float32'), geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO2, epsg=4326)) print('field:', FIELD.rows, 'x', FIELD.columns)
    field: 80 x 120

    1. Line chart — charts.line¶

    An x–y line/marker plot. A 2-D y draws one line per column (e.g. ensemble members).

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 100)
y = np.column_stack([np.sin(x), np.cos(x)])
ax = charts.line(x, y, label=['sin', 'cos'])
ax.legend(); ax.set_title('line() — two series')
ax.figure;
    x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 100) y = np.column_stack([np.sin(x), np.cos(x)]) ax = charts.line(x, y, label=['sin', 'cos']) ax.legend(); ax.set_title('line() — two series') ax.figure;

    2. Bar chart — charts.bar¶

    A single-series bar chart (e.g. monthly totals).

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    months = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun']
ax = charts.bar(range(len(months)), [5, 7, 6, 9, 12, 14], color='C2')
ax.set_xticks(range(len(months))); ax.set_xticklabels(months)
ax.set_title('bar() — monthly values')
ax.figure;
    months = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'] ax = charts.bar(range(len(months)), [5, 7, 6, 9, 12, 14], color='C2') ax.set_xticks(range(len(months))); ax.set_xticklabels(months) ax.set_title('bar() — monthly values') ax.figure;

    3. Histogram — charts.histogram¶

    Histogram of a raster's values. A pyramids Dataset is read over its first band with nodata dropped.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    fig, ax, hist = charts.histogram(FIELD, bins=20, color=['#1f77b4'])
ax.set_title('histogram() — field value distribution'); ax.set_xlabel('value')
fig;
    fig, ax, hist = charts.histogram(FIELD, bins=20, color=['#1f77b4']) ax.set_title('histogram() — field value distribution'); ax.set_xlabel('value') fig;

    4. Vector field + reference arrow — Map.quiver / Map.quiverkey¶

    quiverkey draws the labelled reference arrow for the most recent quiver layer so the field is scaleable.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=4326, figsize=(7, 5))
m.imshow(FIELD, cmap='YlGnBu')
m.quiver(U, V)
m.quiverkey(1.0, '1 unit', x=0.9, y=1.03)
m.set_title('quiver + quiverkey')
m.fig;
    m = Map(crs=4326, figsize=(7, 5)) m.imshow(FIELD, cmap='YlGnBu') m.quiver(U, V) m.quiverkey(1.0, '1 unit', x=0.9, y=1.03) m.set_title('quiver + quiverkey') m.fig;

    5. Labels at lon/lat — Map.text / Map.annotate¶

    text/annotate place labels at geographic points: the lon/lat is reprojected to the display CRS, so they land in the right place (and a far-side point on a globe is skipped).

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=4326, figsize=(7, 5))
m.imshow(FIELD, cmap='terrain')
for name, lon_, lat_ in [('Paris', 2.35, 48.85), ('Berlin', 13.4, 52.5), ('Madrid', -3.7, 40.4)]:
    m.text(lon_, lat_, name, ha='center', fontsize=9, color='black')
m.annotate(10.0, 46.5, 'Alps', xytext=(20, 30), textcoords='offset points',
           arrowprops={'arrowstyle': '->'}, fontsize=9)
m.set_title('text() + annotate() at lon/lat')
m.fig;
    m = Map(crs=4326, figsize=(7, 5)) m.imshow(FIELD, cmap='terrain') for name, lon_, lat_ in [('Paris', 2.35, 48.85), ('Berlin', 13.4, 52.5), ('Madrid', -3.7, 40.4)]: m.text(lon_, lat_, name, ha='center', fontsize=9, color='black') m.annotate(10.0, 46.5, 'Alps', xytext=(20, 30), textcoords='offset points', arrowprops={'arrowstyle': '->'}, fontsize=9) m.set_title('text() + annotate() at lon/lat') m.fig;

    6. Background raster — Map.stock_img¶

    stock_img(dataset) draws a backdrop raster beneath the data (low z-order, view preserved). Here the overlaid field has a nodata hole, so the grey backdrop shows through it.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    holed = field.copy()
holed[25:45, 35:70] = -9999.0          # carve a nodata rectangle
HOLED = Dataset.from_array(arr=holed, geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO, epsg=4326))   # nodata defaults to -9999
backdrop = Dataset.from_array(
    arr=(np.zeros_like(field) + np.linspace(0, 30, nx)).astype('float32'),
    geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO, epsg=4326),
)
m = Map(crs=4326, figsize=(7, 5))
m.stock_img(backdrop, cmap='Greys')    # backdrop, drawn beneath everything
m.imshow(HOLED, cmap='viridis')        # data with a hole -> backdrop shows through
m.set_title('stock_img() backdrop visible through the data hole')
m.fig;
    holed = field.copy() holed[25:45, 35:70] = -9999.0 # carve a nodata rectangle HOLED = Dataset.from_array(arr=holed, geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO, epsg=4326)) # nodata defaults to -9999 backdrop = Dataset.from_array( arr=(np.zeros_like(field) + np.linspace(0, 30, nx)).astype('float32'), geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=GEO, epsg=4326), ) m = Map(crs=4326, figsize=(7, 5)) m.stock_img(backdrop, cmap='Greys') # backdrop, drawn beneath everything m.imshow(HOLED, cmap='viridis') # data with a hole -> backdrop shows through m.set_title('stock_img() backdrop visible through the data hole') m.fig;

    6b. Labelled contours — Map.contour(labels=True)¶

    cleopatra 0.14.0 adds inline contour labels; Map.contour(labels=True) draws them (pass label_kw to tune fmt/fontsize). contourf ignores labels (filled contours aren't line-labelled). The unstructured equivalent Map.tricontour(labels=True) labels triangulated line contours the same way (cleopatra 0.15.0).

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    m = Map(crs=4326, figsize=(7, 5))
m.contourf(FIELD, cmap='YlGnBu', levels=10)
m.contour(FIELD, levels=10, cmap='gray', labels=True, label_kw={'fmt': '%.0f', 'fontsize': 8})
m.set_title('contour(labels=True) — inline isoline labels')
m.fig;
    m = Map(crs=4326, figsize=(7, 5)) m.contourf(FIELD, cmap='YlGnBu', levels=10) m.contour(FIELD, levels=10, cmap='gray', labels=True, label_kw={'fmt': '%.0f', 'fontsize': 8}) m.set_title('contour(labels=True) — inline isoline labels') m.fig;

    7. Multi-panel layout — grid + shared_colorbar¶

    grid(nrows, ncols) returns one figure and a Map per cell; shared_colorbar adds a single colorbar spanning the panels.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    fig, maps = grid(2, 2, crs=4326, figsize=(9, 7))
im = None
for k, m in enumerate(maps):
    im = m.imshow(FIELD, cmap='RdYlBu_r', vmin=0, vmax=30)
    m.set_title(f'panel {k}')
shared_colorbar(fig, im, maps, label='value')
fig.suptitle('grid(2, 2) with a shared colorbar')
fig;
    fig, maps = grid(2, 2, crs=4326, figsize=(9, 7)) im = None for k, m in enumerate(maps): im = m.imshow(FIELD, cmap='RdYlBu_r', vmin=0, vmax=30) m.set_title(f'panel {k}') shared_colorbar(fig, im, maps, label='value') fig.suptitle('grid(2, 2) with a shared colorbar') fig;
